title: A massive stellar bulge in a regularly rotating galaxy 1.2 billion years after the Big Bang
question: Test galaxy formation and bulge assembly scenarios at $z\simeq5$ by spatially resolving the cold gas distribution, kinematics, and mass components of the starburst AGN-host galaxy ALESS 073.1.

data.sensitivity: 18 uJy beam^-1 (continuum); 0.18 mJy beam^-1 per ~28 km s^-1 channel ([C II] cube)

what.value: Molecular gas mass of $(1.6 \pm 0.3) \times 10^{10}$ M$_\odot$ from CO($J=2\rightarrow1$) line detection

evidence.quote: The galaxy has been detected in the CO($J=2\rightarrow1$) line giving a molecular gas mass of $(1.6 \pm 0.3) \times 10^{10}$ M$_\odot$ (cite: Coppin2010).

what.value: Atomic gas mass of $(4.7 \pm 0.5)\times10^{9}$ M$_\odot$ inferred from CO($J=2\rightarrow1$) and [C II] fluxes using PDR models

evidence.quote: The mass of atomic gas (hydrogen and helium) can be inferred from the CO($J=2\rightarrow1$) and \[C II\] fluxes using models of photo-dissociation regions (PDR), giving a value of $(4.7 \pm 0.5)\times10^{9}$ M$_\odot$ (cite: DeBreuck2011; DeBreuck2014).

what.value: Six independent SED-fitting estimates of total stellar mass ranging from 5 to $13\times10^{10}$ M$_\odot$ (average $10^{11}$ M$_\odot$)

evidence.quote: The total stellar mass ($M_\star$) of ALESS 073.1 has been estimated by six different teams by fitting the spectral energy distribution (SED) with stellar population synthesis models (cite: Stark2007; Coppin2009; Wardlow2011; Gilli2014; Simpson2014; Wiklind2014).
We adopt the arithmetic average of the six independent determinations ($10^{11}$ M$_\odot$) as our initial guess.

external_data.citation: (cite: Stark2007; Coppin2009; Wardlow2011; Gilli2014; Simpson2014; Wiklind2014)

what.value: Stellar mass-halo mass relation at $z=4.5-5.5$ with 0.45 dex scatter

evidence.quote: which we derive from data at $z=4.5-5.5$ (cite: Legrand2019).
We assume a scatter of 0.45 dex in halo mass at fixed stellar mass (cite: Legrand2019).

what.value: Halo concentration prior at $z>3$ centered at $C_{200} = 3.4$ with standard deviation of 25%

evidence.quote: The halo concentration ($C_{200}$) becomes nearly independent of halo mass at $z>3$, thus we assume a Gaussian prior centered at $C_{200} = 3.4$ with a standard deviation of 25$\%$ (cite: Dutton2014).

what.value: Kinematic measurements at $z<3.5$ and semi-empirical model predictions based on Toomre's disk instability parameter for Fig. 3

evidence.quote: The gas velocity dispersion of ALESS 073.1 is consistent with the extrapolations from data at $z<3.5$ (Fig. 3A) but lies at the low $\sigma_{\rm V}$ boundary of the prediction of a semi-empirical model based on Toomre's disk instability parameter (cite: Wisnioski2015), despite the galaxy hosts a starburst and a dust-obscured AGN.
We thank L. Legrand and H. Übler for providing tabular data from their publications.

recipe.goal: Calibrate, reweight, and image ALMA continuum and dirty [C II] data cube, then continuum-subtract and clean the cube in GIPSY
recipe.method: Calibrate Fourier-plane data with standard CASA pipeline, harmonize visibility weights on line-free channels with oldstatwt, regrid line data to 15.626 MHz channels, image continuum and dirty line cube with Hogbom deconvolver and Briggs robust=0.5, subtract first-order polynomial continuum in image plane in GIPSY, clean within a 3 sigma smoothed Boolean mask down to 3 sigma_d, and apply Hanning spectral smoothing
key_parameters: 102 channels of 15.626 MHz (~14 km s^-1) width; Hanning smoothed to ~28 km s^-1
Briggs robust = 0.5; Boolean mask smoothed to 0.4'' clipped at 3 sigma_s; cleaned to 3 sigma_d

recipe.goal: Construct moment maps and model 3D [C II] gas kinematics to derive surface brightness profile, rotation curve, and velocity dispersion profile
recipe.method: Construct moment maps using smooth & search option in 3DBAROLO; fit 3D tilted-ring rotating disk model to the [C II] cube in three runs: (1) estimate center (x0, y0), PA, and V_sys as ring averages; (2) fix PA=40 deg and estimate average inclination i; (3) fit V_rot and sigma_V with geometric parameters fixed
key_parameters: z_0 = 300 pc (fixed); V_rad = 0 (fixed); PA = 40 deg (fixed after run 1); i = 25 +/- 3 deg (from run 2)
assumptions: Planck 2018 LambdaCDM cosmology (Omega_m = 0.315, Omega_Lambda = 0.685, H_0 = 67.4 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, 0.1'' = 657.7 pc at z = 4.7555); fully axisymmetric disk model with azimuthal averages for surface density; negligible radial motions (V_rad = 0)

recipe.goal: Model 2D dust continuum morphology and HST rest-frame UV bulge size with GALFIT
recipe.method: Fit 2D exponential disk (Sersic n=1) to ALMA dust continuum map in GALFIT with iterative 5 sigma residual masking; fit HST F160W image in GALFIT using a 7-star PSF to obtain upper limit on bulge effective radius R_e
key_parameters: Gaussian PSF = 0.123'' x 0.095'' at PA = -63.9 deg for ALMA continuum; Sersic index n = 1, projected axis ratio = 0.9, center fixed to [C II] disk; 5 iterations of >5 sigma residual masking

recipe.goal: Compute gravitational circular velocity contributions of individual mass components and fit dynamical mass models to the rotation curve via MCMC
recipe.method: Compute circular velocity profiles for cold gas disk, stellar disk, stellar bulge, and NFW DM halo using GIPSY task Rotmod; fit 4-component fiducial mass model (and 3-component alternatives) to the rotation curve using EMCEE MCMC sampler
key_parameters: Gas and stellar disk exponential vertical scale height = 300 pc; stellar disk exponential radial scale length = 700 pc; bulge De Vaucouleurs R_e = 300 pc; component reference mass = 10^10 M_sun
EMCEE: 200 walkers, 1000 burn-in iterations, 2000 production iterations, stretch move parameter a = 2
assumptions: [C II] radial profile traces cold gas disk; dust continuum radial profile traces stellar disk; spherical De Vaucouleurs bulge includes central SMBH (<10% mass); spherical NFW DM halo; abundance-matching stellar-to-halo mass relation log(M_200) = 0.73 log(M_*) + 4.61; CO-to-H2 alpha_CO = 0.8 M_sun (K km s^-1 pc^2)^-1 and PDR atomic gas mass used for gas mass prior

evidence.quote: The PA is then fixed to 40$^{\circ}$ because the velocity field does not show any strong indication for a warped disk within $R\simeq0.45''$.
A second run of $^{\rm 3D}$BAROLO is used to estimate an average inclination of $25^{\circ}\pm3^{\circ}$; the uncertainty is taken to be the standard deviation across the rings.

answer_key.quantity: [C II] disk rotation velocity (V_rot) at i = 22 deg

evidence.quote: For the best-fitting inclination of 22$^{\circ}$, the \[C II\] disk rotates at velocities ($V_{\rm rot}$) of 300 to 400 km s$^{-1}$ (Fig. 2A).

answer_key.quantity: Intrinsic velocity dispersion (sigma_V) at small radii

evidence.quote: The intrinsic velocity dispersion ($\sigma_{V}$) reaches 50 to 60 km s$^{-1}$ at small radii and decreases to $\sim$10 km s$^{-1}$ in the outer parts (Fig. 2C).

answer_key.quantity: Intrinsic velocity dispersion (sigma_V) in outer parts

evidence.quote: The intrinsic velocity dispersion ($\sigma_{V}$) reaches 50 to 60 km s$^{-1}$ at small radii and decreases to $\sim$10 km s$^{-1}$ in the outer parts (Fig. 2C).

answer_key.quantity: Ratio of rotation velocity to velocity dispersion (V_rot / sigma_V) within 2.5 kpc

evidence.quote: The ratio of rotation velocity to velocity dispersion (Fig. 2D) is $\sim$10 within 2.5 kpc, similar to that of cold gas disks at $z=0$ (cite: Wisnioski2015).

answer_key.quantity: Upper limit on large-scale radial motions (V_rad)

evidence.quote: If we leave $V_{\rm rad}$ as a free parameter, we find values consistent with zero within the uncertainties, so we conclude that large-scale radial motions in the disk must be smaller than $\sim$30 km s$^{-1}$ (approximately the velocity resolution).

answer_key.quantity: Dust disk position angle (PA) from GALFIT (5th iteration)

evidence.quote: GALFIT returns $\rm{PA}=41^{\circ}\pm5^{\circ}$ at the first iteration and $\rm{PA}=36^{\circ}\pm6^{\circ}$ at the fifth, final iteration (Fig. S4B).
The azimuthally-averaged radial density profile from the ALMA continuum map can be described by an exponential model with a scale length of 700 pc (Fig. 2B).

answer_key.quantity: Bulge effective radius (R_e) upper limit from HST F160W

evidence.quote: The galaxy is unresolved, but we obtain an upper limit on $R_{\rm e}$ of about 300 pc (less than one HST pixel).

answer_key.quantity: DM halo circular velocity (V_200) from MCMC
Total baryonic mass within 3.5 kpc (M_baryon) from MCMC

evidence.quote: We obtain a bulge-to-total mass ratio $M_{\rm bul}/M_{\rm baryon} = 0.44$, where $M_{\rm baryon}$ is given by the sum of all baryonic (non-DM) components within 3.5 kpc.

not_stated_but_needed: Exact CASA version and pipeline version used for calibration and imaging
GIPSY version used for continuum subtraction, cleaning, and Rotmod
Exact frequency/channel ranges defined as line-free channels for oldstatwt, continuum imaging, and image-plane polynomial continuum subtraction
Image cell size (pixel scale) and image dimensions (in pixels) for continuum map and [C II] cube
Whether primary beam correction was applied to the continuum map and [C II] cube
Best-fitting kinematic center coordinates (x_0, y_0) and systemic velocity (V_sys) determined in the first 3DBAROLO run
missing_for_reproduction: Exact CASA and GIPSY software versions
Exact channel/frequency ranges used to define line-free channels for oldstatwt and image-plane continuum subtraction
Best-fitting kinematic center coordinates (x_0, y_0) and systemic velocity (V_sys) used in 3DBAROLO (though recoverable from supplementary FITS files Data S1-S6)
Custom Python script wrapping GIPSY Rotmod and EMCEE for the MCMC mass modeling
score_reason: Exceptionally thorough methods description (imaging, 3DBAROLO ring setup, GALFIT parameters, Rotmod assumptions, and full MCMC likelihood/priors/sampler settings) combined with public raw data and complete supplementary FITS cubes, moment maps, and mass model tables (Data S1-S8).
rediscovery_reason: All raw ALMA datasets and processed FITS cubes/maps are publicly available, the 3DBAROLO and MCMC mass-modeling recipes are explicitly parameterized, and the main claims rest on well-defined numeric outputs (rotation curve, V_rot/sigma_V, component masses, and M_bul/M_baryon).
